question: The Pozzilli incinerator and the Sesto Campano cement works are located in near one another on the plain of Venafro. According to the Chair of the Molise association of doctors for the Environment (ISDE) the neurocardiovascular and chronic respiratory diseases suffered in the region are linked to the amount of nitrogen oxides (NOx) and fine particles (PM2.5) in the atmosphere1.

An epidemiological study released by the Municipality of Venafro on 3 August 2022 revealed the prevalence of cardiovascular diseases that could be correlated with the high cadmium levels found by the Isernia Public Prosecutor's Office2. Fine particle studies for June, July and December 2021 were followed by a delayed report from ISPRA on the subject.

Areas contaminated by cadmium are residential zones of which parts are used for wheat and olive farming, but no public body has intervened to protect the environment and health. The chief prosecutor at the Isernia court has uncovered critical faults in the emission-monitoring system.
The Pozzilli sewage works and the Colacem and HERAmbiente plants have also been found to be in breach of their environmental impact assessments3. In view of this: 1.
Will the Commission check compliance with Articles 8, 15, 16 and 17 of Directive 2010/75/EU and Article 6 of Directive 2004/35/EC in the Molise region?
Does it have up-to-date data on the cancer registry in Isernia?
answer: 1. To operate, the waste incineration as well as cement plants at stake which fall in the scope of Annex I of the Industrial Emissions Directive (IED) (4) must hold a permit granted in compliance with the IED and the relevant Best Available Techniques conclusions (5). In addition, Italy is under the obligation to meet air quality standards throughout its territor y (6).

The Environmental Liability Directive (7) (ELD) requires in its Article 6 that operators who caused an environmental damage take steps to limit or prevent further damage and take the required remedial measures, and that competent authorities ensure that such obligations are implemented.

The Commission closely monitors the implementation of relevant EU legislation and, when persistent and structural breaches of EU legislation occur, they are followed up, including through infringement procedures (8). On the basis of the information provided, the Commission is unable to identify persistent and structural breaches of EU legislation.

As announced under the Zero Pollution Action Plan (10), the new European Cancer Inequalities Registry (ECIR) (11) integrates indicators on environmental risk factors for cancer and associated burden . Almost all the European population-based cancer registries are members of the European Network of Cancer Registries (ENCR ) (12).

The province of Isernia is included in the Cancer registry of Molise, which is however not yet part of the ENCR; therefore historical data from that registry is not yet available in the European Cancer Information System (ECIS) (13).
